invariant: `Db` MUST be the one high-level facade over a node's SQLite store: applications, bindings and sync read and write through it, with no second query or write path, and it MUST validate a user `Query` into a `PreparedQuery` (its shape and binding) before executing a read or subscription, refusing an invalid query with a typed error.
`Db::upsert` MUST merge the supplied cells over the row's current cells when the row exists, and MUST insert the supplied cells, defaulting the rest, when it does not.

`Db::delete` MUST soft-delete the row: its current version is marked deleted and the image it replaces moves to history, so the row is absent from current reads and subscriptions while history and `includeDeleted` reads still see it.

`Db::restore` MUST refuse a row that is not deleted (`WriteRejected`), and MUST restore a deleted row with the supplied cells, applying column defaults to omitted columns; empty content restores a row whose nullable columns read NULL.

Every standalone write MUST return a `WriteHandle` naming the affected `RowUuid` (generated, or the caller's) and the commit seq of the version it left, and the write MUST be durable in the node's store when the call returns.

A replica's local write MUST commit to its own store at its own node's position (after every server version) and be queued for upload; only the global authority's fate makes it Global. A replica with no server MAY order its sessions' commits, but those fates stay Local.

Waiting for a transaction at `Local` MUST complete once it is committed locally. A `Global` wait MUST complete only when the global authority's fate accepts it (a relay's or a serverless replica's fate does not), MUST fail with the authority's rejection error, and stays pending, not failed, while the upstream is detached or unreachable.

`Transport` MUST be non-blocking: `try_recv() == None` means no message is staged and MUST NOT be read as a disconnect. A link ends only when the host detaches it or `take_failure` reports a frame it cannot decode; then a client detaches from that upstream and a server closes that session, and the database keeps running.
`Db::connect_upstream` MUST carry already-registered facade subscriptions upstream immediately by placing their `(ValidatedQuery, Binding)` pairs into the connection's pending set.
A subscription on a replica MUST attach its query upstream on the next tick when connected, and a subscription made while offline MUST attach once an upstream connects.

A replica MUST attach each upstream subscription once, as its query and binding (`SyncMessage::Subscribe`), and the server MUST serve it under the link's identity; live results with the same shape and binding share one maintained execution while each subscription delivers its own events.

`Db::open` MUST open a partial replica. A history-complete fate authority MUST be opened explicitly (`Db::open_history_complete` or `set_authority`); only the authority assigns server seqs and Global fates, and a replica without a server only orders its own sessions' commits.
A replica MUST upload each pending commit once per connection, in commit order, and resend the unsettled ones after a reconnect or restart; the authority MUST apply a resent commit at most once.
A server MUST serve a subscriber link's reads, and check its commits, under the identity it admitted for that link (`accept_subscriber`), never under the server's own identity.
`Db::tick()` MUST service the upstream link and every subscriber link: apply what each has received and send what each owes, so one failing or slow link does not stall the others.

A failing link MUST NOT fail the node: a peer frame that does not decode ends that link only (a client detaches from its upstream, a server closes the session), the database and its other links keep running, and the host reconnects. A client binding tick driver MUST classify `Db::tick()` failures. A recoverable condition (backpressure, a protocol or transaction conflict, a not-yet-observed read) MUST NOT terminate the driver; it retries with bounded backoff. A fatal failure (storage, schema, an unreadable store), or a recoverable one that outlasts the bounded retries, MUST stop the driver and be surfaced to every caller as an error rather than appearing as a stalled sync operation.
The query builder exposed through `Db::table` MUST support OR/AND/NOT predicates, `contains`, `in_list`, `is_null`, optional and required includes, select, order, limit, and offset.

`Db::mergeable_tx()` MUST commit its writes as one SQLite transaction: readers, local or synced, see all of them or none, a crash keeps all or none of them, and a commit whose fan-out spans several wire frames applies whole.

`Db::serializable_tx()` MUST read at its snapshot and commit only if every read result and written row is unchanged at the authority; a conflict fails the commit (`TransactionConflict` at the replica, `SerializationConflict` from the authority) and applies none of its writes.

Permission advice is a three-valued dry run: `Allowed`/`Denied` are definitive only when issued by the history-complete serving authority, which runs the action under the authenticated link subject's policies (or a session a trusted backend acts for) and rolls it back; a replica without a connected authority, a replica asked as a server, a cancelled request or a timed-out one MUST yield `Unknown`. Advice MUST NOT create or alter rows, reserve a later write, or disclose supporting rows, policy reasons or hidden facts: an answer carries only its request id and verdict. Each request MUST have a fresh id, also across a reopened database; cancellation removes the waiter and keeps an unsent request from being sent, and a late or replayed answer MUST NOT resolve another request. The serving side keeps no per-request state, so replayed requests cost it nothing.

A write's provenance author and its permission subject MUST be the same unless a trusted party attributes it: an attributed write keeps the writer as policy subject and the attributed author as provenance, and an authority MUST refuse a commit whose author differs from a session link's identity ("attribution requires a trusted serving node"); a session link's writes on behalf of other sessions are checked as the link.
`Db::read` MUST be a synchronous read of the local store that never waits for upstream sync; `Db::all` MUST take its semantics from `ReadOpts` (tier and first-load wait).

Reopening persistent storage with the same `DbIdentity` MUST schedule every locally originated transaction that reached `Local` durability and has not reached terminal settlement for upstream delivery. Locally originated means `TxId.node == DbIdentity.node` and `Transaction.made_by == DbIdentity.author`; delivery is at-least-once by `TxId` and relies on idempotent authority handling.

`Db::disconnect` MUST mark the `Db` intentionally offline, disconnect every schema client from its server transport, and leave the local runtime and store alive; `Db::reconnect` MUST clear that marker and reconnect every schema client. A schema client created while intentionally offline MUST remain offline until `reconnect`.

`ReadOpts.tier` selects read behavior: `LocalOnly` reads the node's store and pending writes and asks nothing upstream (a relay serves it from its own store); `LocalFirst` also requests upstream results while delivering local data; `Remote` returns only an authority-confirmed result and never lists pending local versions, waiting while offline. Offline `LocalFirst` reads return locally known data.

A replica MUST keep a pending upload, across reconnects and restarts, until the global authority's fate for it arrives: an acceptance or a rejection. Local persistence, a relay's acknowledgement and a lost fate MUST NOT release it.

An explicit-id insert MUST only create: an insert whose id names a live or deleted row MUST be refused (`WriteRejected`) without publishing a row, and when two serializable transactions both find an id absent and insert it the later commit MUST conflict (`TransactionConflict`), never fail with a storage error. A target hidden by read policy MUST be refused the same way as an upsert over it, without disclosing it.
`ReadOpts.tier` MUST be `ReadTier::LocalOnly`, `ReadTier::LocalFirst`, or `ReadTier::Remote`; no other tier decodes. Pending-write visibility follows this choice.
`ReadOpts::default()` MUST use `ReadTier::LocalFirst` and deliver the local opening without a server wait (`FirstLoad::Deliver`).

`Db::subscribe` MUST deliver live results at the requested tier from the same compiled query as a one-shot read. A `LocalFirst` or `LocalOnly` subscription includes the node's own pending writes and publishes its local opening, empty or not, unless a first-load wait holds it, while `LocalFirst` also attaches upstream; a `Remote` subscription never lists pending local versions. After every commit a maintained result MUST equal a fresh read of the same query.

Subscription streams MUST expose an opening and then add, update and remove events for result rows, computed by re-running the subscription's query on commits that touch its dependency tables and diffing against the delivered result; a removal names the row that left.
`Db::insert` MUST generate the row id from its configured `RowIdSource`; an insert with a caller-supplied `RowUuid` MUST use that id.
`Db::update` MUST preserve omitted columns by merging the patch over the row's current cells.

compared systems and retained runs use identical declared link profiles. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
headline metrics are reported against at least one floor/ceiling/reference anchor. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

Every retained benchmark line MUST include scenario, driver, seed, profile, git_sha, git_dirty, git_status_available, hostname, and knobs. git_status_available is true only when git status --porcelain succeeds and stdout is valid UTF-8; unavailable status MUST be reported dirty, independently of HEAD resolution. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
deterministic scenario runs must assert oracle equality or explicit security counters before reporting success. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
forbidden rows/deltas delivered to an unauthorized client must be exactly zero. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
accepted jazz schedules replayed against SQLite must produce identical final state for S4 reference runs. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

S5 must model append streams as full content: bytes rewrites in streamDocs, not a userland event log, and compare against fsync append-log, SQLite WAL, and zstd anchors. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
Every `branchBy` entry MUST name a non-null, key-encodable ordinary column; same-named branch columns across tables MUST have the same type and canonical encoding.
A content write MUST NOT imply restoration; an inherited or head-key `Deleted` winner remains effective until an explicit `Restored` winner supersedes it.

A base source MUST be either live current state or the exact state of the selected branch key at a supplied `SnapshotRef`; the cut applies consistently to every table and policy dependency in the read.
The canonical read/subscription identity MUST include normalized head and base branch sources, including any snapshot cut.
Normal references MUST resolve a `RowUuid` through the current effective branch view; branch-qualified row references are a separate, unsupported capability.
A view-relative mutation of an inherited row MUST copy-on-write into the head branch key. An exact mutation MUST name its branch key explicitly.

A branch-view read MUST return each row as its head layer supplies it when the head holds the row and as its base supplies it otherwise, with ordinary branch columns reading the head's values; the stored version keeps the branch key it was written under.
Transactions MAY atomically contain versions in multiple branch keys, but admission, fate, persistence, and rejection remain all-or-nothing.

One transaction MAY write rows of several branch keys atomically, but a reader's results and synced rows MUST contain only what its own branch view and read policy select: a sibling branch's rows never reach it because one transaction wrote both.

Read and write policy MUST use ordinary branch columns and the same effective branch view as the operation (one cut for a frozen base and its policy dependencies); missing reference or policy evidence fails closed, and Jazz MUST NOT impose a built-in branch-row existence or lifecycle gate.

Schema evolution MAY only add a `branchBy` column, as a new column with an immutable typed default declared in the schema. Rows written before it, their history, and selectors of versions that do not name it MUST normalize to that default: a branch column at its default is left out of the stored branch key, so they keep their branch and every node, on either version, keys them alike. Making an existing column a branch column, adding one without a default, changing a branch column's default or type, renaming one, or (in the version made current) removing one MUST fail as not supported yet and leave the store unchanged. Except for removal, which is checked against the current version when a version is made current, this holds against every version the store has admitted, in any session, whether the new one opens the store, is activated or admitted, or is registered as a schema view; a lens may not add a branch column with a default other than the declared one; so MUST changing any stored column's type in place.
The logical branch-local row key MUST be `(PhysicalTableId, BranchKey, RowUuid)` while application object identity remains `RowUuid`.

Rows MUST be unique per (id, branch key) and every declared index of a branched table MUST lead with the branch key `_b` and end with `id`, so a branch-view read seeks one branch at a time; this layout is part of the pinned storage format.

A first write to a head row inherited from a branch view's base MUST copy the base row, the current base or the frozen base as of its cut, into the head and apply the write over it, at the authority as at the writer; a row absent from the frozen base at its cut MUST be refused, also after the base table was renamed.
Every row version of a branched table MUST be stored under the complete canonical branch key (`_b`) its branch columns encode, and its history stays under that key.

Branch columns MUST be immutable after insertion: an update that would move a row to another branch key is refused. Moving an object between branch keys requires explicit writes to both branch-local rows, which MAY share one atomic transaction.
Content and deletion histories and current winners MUST be selected independently per `(PhysicalTableId, BranchKey, RowUuid, Layer)`.
Secondary indices MUST be physically prefixed by the exact branch key; a composed branch view MUST apply head/base masking before consulting or publishing index results.
A table with no branch columns MUST behave as shared data in every branch view.
A read selector MUST use globally named branch-column values and each table MUST project that selector onto its declared subset; equal projected head/base branch keys collapse to one source.

A branch-view read MUST let a head row, live or deleted, mask the base row before predicates or relational operators apply, including on indexed reads and for head rows an older schema reader cannot see.

Node-local state MUST NOT be shipped as replicated row payload: a row image carries the row's cells and provenance as values, never the SQLite `rid`, interned author codes, local seqs, or a replica's pending and shadow bookkeeping.

Large values MUST have one implementation, jazz-db's chunk store over `jazz_types::large_values`: every read, edit and sync path goes through it, and a chunked value reads as its logical value. Queries compare a chunked value by cell, never by content (SPEC 19.5).
`delta(a, b)` MUST return edits that turn a's value into b's, at a cost that follows the change, not the value.
A partial selection (a byte, UTF-16 or UTF-8 range, or a JSON pointer) MUST read and pull only the chunks its part covers, at every hop, and MUST follow edits to the value without fetching more.

A subscription's splices for an updated row MUST turn the column's value in the row's previous result into its new value; when they cannot be computed the row carries none and the reader takes the value whole.

A version's chunked cell MUST be immutable: `(epoch, n)` always names the same logical value however the epoch grows, since edits are only ever appended and an epoch's first `count` edits are never rewritten while any cell names them.

Nodes and edits MUST be disclosed only through a row version the reader may read that reaches them: a pull is answered only for a readable version that holds the pulled root and only with nodes of that tree, a synced tree is admitted only for nodes the writer possesses (under a readable version it names or pushed under its own receipt), and content hashes, cached nodes or other rows' roots authorize nothing. The server never reveals whether it holds a node.

Staging chunks (a streamed upload or pushed nodes) MUST NOT create readable application state, authorize a mutation, or publish a root: a failed or rejected publication publishes no row and releases what it staged, and unreferenced pushes are released when their receipt expires.

Only an ordinarily authorized insert or update of the owning row may add edits to an epoch or publish a new large-value root, through the one admission path that checks every descriptor against its tree and every synced tree against what its writer possesses; a caller-authored descriptor MUST be rejected.

Tree nodes MUST be content-addressed by their object hash and stored policy blind in `_jazz_lv_*` tables, so equal content in one store is stored once; a row's read policy is the only gate on them. An absent node is demand to fetch, never an answer.

Epoch ids, cells and materializations MUST NOT cross the wire: a large value crosses as inline bytes, as a tree reference whose nodes are pulled through a readable version (a range read's whole path in one round trip) or pushed before the commit that references them (all but those under the trees of the version the commit names as its source), or as edits extending a version of the same row the receiver holds, named by its seq; a receiver lacking that version asks for the row whole. A read sent after a commit the ingress limit holds back is held with it when it could observe that commit, while reads that cannot observe it are served ahead.
Collection MUST never remove an epoch or node that a retained row version, a staging lease or a receipt reaches.

A chunk store MUST hold only node bytes: a node's metadata (hash, edges, reference counts, receipts, leases) commits with the rows that reference it in SQLite whatever holds its bytes. Only settled leaves move; a leaf's bytes leave the SQLite file only after the chunk store acknowledged its put, are deleted from the chunk store only after the reclamation that frees them committed (a put in flight when its leaf is reclaimed is deleted after it lands), and are verified against their hash on every read. A store that moved leaves MUST refuse to open without its chunk store, and a read of a leaf an asynchronous chunk store holds waits for it, never answers without it.
Wire identities MUST use canonical 16-byte UUIDs (row ids, node ids) and canonical author subjects; per-database author codes and other node-local handles MUST NOT be part of wire identity.
A merge strategy declaration MUST name an existing user column of the containing `TableSchema`.
A table read or write policy, when present, MUST name the table it is attached to and MUST validate against the complete `JazzSchema`.

Each Jazz table MUST be stored as a current table holding one row per (id, branch key) with its commit seq `_seq` and state bits `_st` (bit 0: no content, bit 1: deleted), and a history table `<table>__h` keyed by (id, branch key, seq) holding every superseded committed image.

A delete or restore MUST be a new version of the row that sets or clears the deleted bit of `_st` and keeps the content it hides; history marks with the no-content bit of `_st` the versions whose commit wrote no content, so history reads list content versions and every version reads its row's current deletion.
The unit of replication MUST be a row image: table, row id, branch key, server seq, deleted and content flags, and the row's cells by column name, with provenance authors as canonical subjects.
A write MUST move the row's committed current version to history before changing it, and only committed images enter history: versions written earlier in the same commit are not superseded history.

Each current table MUST be unique per (id, branch key) and carry a `_seq` index; its only other indexes are the schema's declared ones (`<table>__ix(...)`), created when a schema activates and filled from existing rows.

The authority MUST give every accepted commit one global seq, strictly increasing and stored on each version it writes (`_seq`), so history, as-of cuts and resumed subscriptions (`since`) are seq ranges; a reopened store, or a fresh one under a reused node, continues above its floor.

Authors MUST be interned per database in `_jazz_authors`, one code per (account, issuer, subject), and every read, egress and sync path MUST resolve codes back to the author record; codes never leave their database.

Opening a store MUST create the fixed `_jazz_*` system tables, stamp a new file's storage format or check an existing one's, and create each application table of the active schema (current and history tables, declared indexes, large-value triggers); activating a newer schema only adds tables, columns and indexes.

Every sync message MUST have one canonical postcard spelling: a frame with trailing bytes, or one that does not decode, is rejected, and the receiver ends that link rather than repairing the message or panicking. Every frame of the pinned wire corpus decodes to its variant and re-encodes to its exact bytes.

A mergeable commit MUST carry only its writes; a serializable commit also carries its snapshot cut and every read it made, and only serializable commits are validated against reads. A mergeable commit is never rejected because rows it did not read changed.

The authority's current row MUST be its post-image after the last commit it accepted for that row, with superseded images in history; rejected and pending commits MUST NOT become a settled image, on the authority or on a replica, through replay or reopen.
Every table MUST expose its generated UUID as id. Explicit table columns named id MUST be rejected regardless of type or nullability; nested enum payload fields named id remain ordinary data.

Persisted system authors MUST use the reserved nil account UUID, urn:jazz:system issuer, and canonical originating node UUID subject; decoding this provenance MUST NOT grant the internal SYSTEM capability. External admission MUST reject the reserved account and issuer.

`TxTime` and `GlobalTime` MUST encode physical milliseconds in the high 46 bits and a logical counter in the low 18 bits. Their unsigned packed order is canonical. Their allocators MUST advance physical time on logical exhaustion and return a typed overflow only after the final packed position.

A commit MUST be identified by its writer's node UUID and the writer's transaction number: the authority records each applied commit's result under that pair and a replica where each settled one landed (`_jazz_transactions`, the node interned in `_jazz_nodes`), so a resent commit is recognised and keeps the writer's transaction id.
`SchemaVersionId` MUST be UUIDv5 over `JazzSchema::canonical_bytes()` in namespace `SCHEMA_VERSION_NAMESPACE`.
Canonical schema identity MUST change when a column's `MergeStrategy` changes.

Structural schema identity MUST recursively encode every portable column type, including payload-enum case and field structure: type tags, declared case and field order, names, field types, and nullability are identity-bearing.

A declared `MergeStrategy::Counter` MUST be accepted only on non-nullable integer columns. Public `Integer` and `BigInt` lower to `I32` and `I64`; internal schemas may use `U8`, `U16`, `U32`, `U64`, `I32`, or `I64`.

node-core work must remain simulation-first. Load-bearing rule: production node semantics are exercised through deterministic inputs and explicit method/event surfaces; no transport, thread, randomness, or clock dependency should be hidden inside node logic. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

crash/restart recovery must rebuild in-memory node discipline state from storage, not from transport/session state. recover_from_storage rebuilds aliases, schema aliases, branch metadata, HLC/global timestamp state, pending edges, and rejected transaction headers (recovery.rs lines 48-180); M3 harness restarts reader/core nodes from storage (support.rs lines 1551-1590). This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

benchmarks are discipline gates that report deterministic counters plus timing ratios, but appendix A should not quote dirty-tree numbers. Sync benchmark emits JSON fields for seed/config, fate RTT, view refresh, version bundle/ref counts, reject counts, and parked-orphan counters (sync.rs lines 300-318). Validation benchmark config uses clients/rows/commits/hot-row percent/seed (validation.rs lines 28-48). This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

Core, clients, and local relays use the same node/message vocabulary rather than separate semantic implementations. Relay ingestion stores pending local units without assigning fate. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

commit/fate/view ingestion must be idempotent and conflict-detecting: a duplicate commit unit with an identical payload is a no-op, a duplicate with a conflicting payload is rejected, applying the same fate twice changes nothing, and a stale pending state cannot regress an accepted fate. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

time-like and state-lattice domains must use distinct types and monotone transitions. Identifiers: GlobalTime, TxTime, Fate, DurabilityTier. GlobalTime::tick explicitly packs physical milliseconds plus a logical counter; accepted core commits atomically persist their timestamp and committed frontier before applying DurabilityTier::Global (ingest.rs lines 513-533); errors include Error::NonMonotoneState and Error::ConflictingFate (node/mod.rs lines 2119-2127). Wire payloads carry VersionRecord data and not local/global-derived currentness (protocol.rs lines 110-140); local current rows live in each table's current table, apart from its `__h` history table (jazz-db `lib.rs`); upstream state is represented on TransactionRecord as fate, global_time, and durability (tx.rs lines 130-149). A `PeerRole::Relay` link MUST authenticate as an explicit relay transport capability, MUST carry no permission subject, and MUST NOT terminate a client identity.

invariant: Fate and durability MUST remain separate axes: local persistence does not imply acceptance. Receivers MUST raise observed durability only from explicit durability claims.

Resubmitting a commit the authority already applied (same writer node and transaction number), after a lost acknowledgement or a restart on either side, MUST return its recorded result and seq without applying it again.
A client cache MUST NOT evict fate-pending units or parked commit families needed to recover outstanding work.
Client refetch after eviction MUST use payload-inventory resubscribe rather than assuming complete local history.

Re-delivering a commit the authority already accepted (a reconnect resend or a relay retry) MUST return its known fate and seq without applying the commit again, whatever it writes: a counter change is counted exactly once, also when other commits were sequenced in between.

A dynamically catalogued serving authority MUST NOT accept an uploaded commit unit before an authority has activated a schema selecting its structural schema and explicit table permissions. If no schema is active, it MUST reject the unit as `Fate::Rejected(RejectionReason::MalformedCommit("permissions_head_missing: no published permissions head"))`, rather than silently accepting or deferring it.

A relay MUST forward its sessions' commits upstream and MUST NOT give them a Global fate: it applies them optimistically, keeps them pending until the authority's fate arrives, and relays that fate, including a refusal, to the session.

A relay MUST report a downstream result as the global authority's (`Settled.global`) only once its own upstream confirmed it, never from its own store alone; with an upstream installed but unanswered it holds the settlement, and with no upstream at all it settles local reads as its own.

A scope-isolated client relay MUST attach foregrounds from exactly one durable authentication scope, MUST remain a non-authority, and MUST serve those foregrounds from retained authorized knowledge without re-evaluating read policy.
implementation: planned scope-isolated relay serving context and browser/RN topology matrix

invariant: Authoritative result state retained by a relay MUST be identified by the complete canonical query identity and exact immutable policy binding; result members, generations, receipts, repair state, and persistence from different policy bindings MUST never share a mutable result identity.
implementation: planned policy-scoped authority-result identity and durable settled-view state

invariant: A scope-isolated client relay MAY answer same-scope row-version repair without re-evaluating policy only for a version in that scope's previously delivered authorized payload closure or a same-scope authored pending version. Other relays MUST prove that exact closure membership or forward repair to an authority.

Application and wire callers MUST NOT choose internal authority-result source identities or policy bindings. The receiving topology assigns and validates them from the authenticated connection and admitted session.
implementation: planned inbound normalization and topology-owned authority-result construction

invariant: A fate authority receiving a commit (mergeable or serializable) through a scope-isolated client relay MUST authorize it only under that relay attachment's immutable server-admitted foreground binding, then pass an internal non-wire proof into terminal admission. Transaction authorship, relay transport, `SYSTEM`, persisted state, stale epochs, and mutable session-claim refresh MUST NOT substitute for or widen that binding.
implementation: planned scope-relay admission capability and terminal authorization proof

invariant: A relay MUST serve sessions of its own identity only: a store configured as a user uploads what its sessions write under its own identity, so serving another user's session would attribute that user's writes to it. Every accept path (the core's `accept_subscriber`, and through it the binding host, the browser worker and the native relay) refuses a session of another identity with reason `identity_mismatch`; a system store (a server) serves any identity. Each accept names the session's own replica author (the browser worker admits a tab as the author it connected with, not the worker's). A server checks the replica's declared identity against the one it authenticated when it admits a link.

A client link MUST be admitted as exactly one author identity, and the server MUST check that link's reads and writes under that identity's policies; a session cannot present an identity other than its link's.

Only the global authority makes a serializable commit's acceptance Global: a relay forwards it for validation and applies it only optimistically meanwhile, and a replica its host says has no server validates its sessions' commits itself, with fates that stay Local.
Once a replica has applied a commit's fate, a resent commit, a duplicate fate or a reconnect MUST NOT reopen or change it.
A row's history MUST be linear: each accepted write makes the next version of the row in authority seq order and supersedes the previous one, so there are never concurrent heads to choose between.

For `MergeStrategy::Counter`, a write MUST travel as its change from the value it saw, and every node applying it MUST add that change to the value it holds, so concurrent changes from the same base sum exactly in any order. A change that would take the counter outside its column type's range MUST be refused rather than wrapped.

Content and deletion state MUST be separate layers: content writes MUST NOT change the deletion state, and a deleted row stays hidden, its history included, until a restore reveals its current content. A write a replica makes over a deletion it already holds, a delete included, is refused (`row already deleted`); a write merged over a deletion it did not see applies underneath it.

A replica MUST install each server image it receives as the row's settled version, in its current table or, while a pending local commit overrides the row, in its history table as the upstream baseline below the replica's local sequence range, so its settled view of the rows it holds equals the authority's.
Re-ingesting the same commit unit with identical version rows in a different order MUST be idempotent and MUST NOT create a conflict.

A rejected commit MUST NOT leave a version anywhere: the authority writes nothing for it, no other replica receives it, and the writer's replica drops it from its rows and history when the rejection arrives.

The authority's post-image MUST be a deterministic function of the accepted writes in seq order: no wall clock, writer clock or other node-local state enters a merged value. Concurrent writes to different cells give the same post-image in any seq order, counter and set changes commute, and when two writes change one plain cell the one the authority sequences last keeps it.
History MUST be per row and branch: a row's history lists only that row's versions in the branch read, in seq order, and no version encodes a dependency on another row, branch or layer.

Among concurrent writes to one plain cell, the write the authority accepts last MUST win, whatever the writers' clocks: a writer whose clock runs ahead gains nothing, and an older offline edit that arrives later wins.

A replica's write over its own unsettled write MUST be accepted and applied after it, in order, over the authority's current row, through relays too; when the earlier write is rejected, every write built on it MUST be rejected too (reason `predecessor_rejected`), since its image carried the rejected write's values.

Whether a write maybe conflicts MUST be derived from the row's accepted history and never stored. A write's base is the version of the row it was built on: an accepted seq, or an unsettled commit (resolved at the authority to the seq it landed at). Its writer saw every version up to a base seq, or a base commit's version and everything that version saw, down the chain. A write is maybe conflicting iff it has a base and an accepted version of the row before it is one its writer never saw; inserts and blind updates are never maybe conflicting. Its conflict analysis MUST be those missed versions whose authored columns overlap the write's. A value-merging column MUST merge a write with its base version's value only when a missed version authored that column, and otherwise keep the write's value as sent.
One replica's commits MUST reach the authority in the order it made them, on every link (through relays, across reconnects and restarts), and the authority MUST apply them in arrival order.

A text-merging column (`MergeStrategy::Text`, `Markdown` or `Html`, declared only on non-nullable string user columns) MUST store a plain string, and writes to it travel as plain values. Only the authority merges: when a version before the write that its writer never saw authored the column, it MUST three-way merge the value its writer last saw of the column (the newest commit on its chain that authored the column, as that commit sent it, or else the accepted version the chain was built on), the value it holds and the write's value at token boundaries: changes to disjoint parts of the base all apply, a change both sides made applies once, inserts at one point go in seq order, overlapping pure inserts and deletes union (as do one side's inserts with the other's replacements), and of two overlapping replacements the write sequenced later wins. Otherwise, or when the merge would spend more than a fixed budget of diff steps, the write's value stands as sent. For a version whose value a merge changed, the authority MUST also keep that version as its writer sent it, flagged as sent in its state bits, and MUST NOT list, sync or read it as a version.

A replica MUST converge to the authority's post-image and never mint a merged version of its own: after concurrent writes every replica, fresh, resynced or subscribed late, reads the authority's result.

For a plain (`MergeStrategy::Lww`) column and for the row's deletion state, the authority MUST apply each accepted write to the row's post-image as a patch in the order it accepts the writes: every cell the write authored takes the write's value (last arrival wins), every cell it did not author keeps the row's value, and nothing a write authored is dropped. Concurrent writes to different cells of one row therefore all apply, and a write that does not author the deletion keeps the row's deletion state, so an edit made over an image older than an accepted delete leaves the row deleted.
`MergeStrategy::Counter` MUST be declared only on non-nullable integer user columns.

A schema version's id MUST be its content address (`schema.version_id()`), and a non-genesis version MUST be admitted with its lineage lens before it is known or writeable: until then a store opened on it refuses writes as "awaiting published catalogue admission", and a deployment with missing artifacts, bad hashes or conflicting migrations is rejected.
A write MUST be stored under the stored names its schema version maps its tables and columns to (`_jazz_names`), whichever admitted version wrote it, so every version reads it back.

A commit authored under an older admitted schema version MUST be applied through that version's names to the same stored rows, by a server whose current schema is newer, without being rejected or rewritten for its version.
Every admitted schema version MUST read the same stored rows: a lens maps names, so the current row and its history are shared, and each version reads them, live and in history, under its own names.

Natural forward/reverse lens projection MUST implement `RenameColumn`, `CopyColumn`, `AddColumn`, and `DropColumn.backwards_default` deterministically, and MUST reject `TransformColumn`/`RejectSourceDelta` during projection.

Reading through lenses MUST commute with writing through them: for writes made under any admitted schema versions, every version reads the same rows under its own names, across several lens hops in either direction.
`ShapeId` MUST include the authored `SchemaVersionId`; identical canonical query bytes against different schema versions MUST produce different shape ids.
A commit MUST NOT be rejected or rewritten solely because its authored schema version differs from the server's current schema version.
`TransformColumn` MUST be accepted only when its transform key is registered as bijective and canonical-equality-preserving; the current registry is identity/no-op only.

Every schema version MUST be governed by the current schema's policies, matched by stored table: a reader or writer on an older version is checked against the stored rows under the current policies, and policies are never translated into an old version.

A published `MigrationLens` MUST have `lens.id == lens.content_id()` and both `lens.source` and `lens.target` MUST be known `SchemaVersionId`s; `content_id()` MUST hash the canonical lens payload and exclude the embedded id field.

Admitted schema versions, their stored-name maps, and the stored tables and columns they use, dropped ones included, MUST NOT be garbage-collected: older versions stay readable after newer ones activate and after reopen.

A store MUST be reopened only by the storage format it was written in: every Jazz SQLite file carries its format in `_jazz_format`, and another format, an unstamped or damaged file, or a pre-SQLite store MUST be refused with a typed error, the file left unchanged.
A stored table or column name MUST never be reused for another logical column: a name freed by a rename gets a new stored column, and a removed and re-added table does not resurface old rows.

A store's deploy catalogue MUST be its typed catalogue tables (`_jazz_schemas`, `_jazz_lenses`, `_jazz_permissions`) with canonical JSON definitions, written in the same transaction as the admission and activation they describe: a change that fails leaves no rows and no in-memory state, a reopened store admits from its own rows without replay, every permissions revision is kept, and a definition that does not parse fails startup rather than recovering a partial catalogue.
Catalogue mutation messages MUST be accepted only from an authenticated catalogue-admin transport/session context; serialized author fields are provenance and MUST NOT grant authority.

Stored rows MUST NOT be tagged with the schema version that wrote them: every admitted version reads and writes the same stored rows through its names, and a link's schema version belongs to its session, not to each row image.

A server MUST hold every message of a session whose declared schema version it has not admitted, commits included, applying none of them, tell the client so (`SchemaAdmission`), and serve the held messages in order once the version is admitted.
A read attached under a schema version the server has not admitted MUST expose no rows while it waits and MUST be answered once the version's lineage lens is published.

The server's current schema selection MUST advance only by a successful activation under a newer revision: a rejected or stale activation leaves the active schema and its revision unchanged, and permissions reconciliation never installs a stale head.
Admitted schema versions, lenses, stored-name maps and the current write schema MUST survive a restart, in a replica's store and in the server's catalogue storage.

Publishing a schema version with its lineage lens MUST be all or nothing: a deployment that fails validation leaves no partial catalogue, the version is not writeable before its lens is admitted, and once admitted its stored tables are grown and its indexes filled before it is used.

Opening a store MUST create the system tables and every application table of the active schema before any read or write, and activating a schema at runtime MUST add its tables, columns and indexes to the live store without a reopen.

A query MUST compile to one parameterized SQL statement per shape with its binding values bound as parameters, and live results with identical SQL and parameters MUST share one execution (a fan-out group) while each binding gets its own results.
Prepared graph lowering MUST reject `!=` predicates against parameters until supported.

A query prepared under one schema version MUST stay valid when another version is admitted or activated: it is recompiled where needed and keeps reading by its own version's names over the shared stored tables, joins and includes included.

Aggregation, ordering, pagination and projection MUST compile into the query's SQL. Ordering is logical, ties break by row id in the last key's direction, grouped aggregates order before their window, and an order key need not be selected.

Synced reads MUST be served by the same compiled query as local reads: the server runs the client's query under the client's identity and ships its result rows plus the supporting rows the query reads (include targets, array children, join and gather edges), keeping them coherent; shapes that read further are refused as not supported yet.
A whole-table subscription MUST be an ordinary query, served like any other with no separate current-rows path, and a replica's synced result for it equals the authority's read of it for that reader.

The authority MUST validate each serializable read by re-running it under the reader's identity at commit and comparing with its result at the snapshot: a phantom entering a predicate or window conflicts, an unrelated write does not.
Counter merge strategy MUST NOT be accepted for nullable or non-integer columns.

Stored columns MUST carry no SQLite type affinity: each value is bound with its own storage class and read back by the column's declared type, so a store opens on any SQLite and values (arrays, bigints beyond the safe range, bytes) round-trip exactly.
Each history table `<table>__h` MUST be keyed by (id, branch key, seq) WITHOUT ROWID, so a row's versions are contiguous and read in seq order by history and as-of reads.

Read and write policies MUST compile to SQL predicates over the same tables as queries: `Exists` is a correlated `EXISTS`, `Inherits` unrolls to its depth bound, a relation `gather` is `WITH RECURSIVE`. A write's policy is checked on the old row (USING) and the new row (WITH CHECK), and inheritance applies the parent's clause for the same operation.

One-shot reads, live subscriptions, synced reads and serializable validation MUST run the same compiled SQL for a query: how a result is delivered is not part of its shape and never selects another evaluator.

A read MUST let SQLite choose its access path over the current table's unique (id, branch key) key and the declared indexes, with policy predicates compiled into the same statement: a read naming row ids seeks them, and a filter or order a declared index serves uses it without a temporary sort.

Position-bounded historical cuts and branch-base reads MUST use the `by_table_global_time` bounded range path when sound, returning the same rows as the full-scan currentness oracle while touching only the requested global-time range.

Permission advice and policy evidence MUST run the ordinary compiled statements: advice dry-runs the action under the session's policies and rolls it back, and a gather policy's seed and steps run as the same recursive SQL a read uses.
A subscription under an older schema version MUST see writes made under a newer one, renamed tables and columns included, as ordinary changes under its own names, without a reset.

A structured (relation) query MUST deliver root rows each carrying its nested relation arrays: a child change reaches the subscriber as an update of its root row, empty relations stay in an ordinary root row, siblings with empty and full relations share one record type, and ordered roots keep their order and window across changes.

A scalar enum's authored discriminant is scoped to its row `SchemaVersionId`; lowering translates it through the persistent case identity of its physical column occurrence before using a local storage tag, predicate, grouping key, ordering key, or projection. Concurrent sibling authored ordinal allocations cannot alias.
Each admitted schema version's stored-name map MUST be kept in `_jazz_names`, one row per (version, table, column) keyed by its admission number in `_jazz_versions`, and read back exactly on reopen.

Node-local integers MUST NOT appear on the wire as identities: commits name their writer node and rows by UUID, authors travel as canonical subjects (never interned codes), and a replica's local seqs never reach the authority as server seqs.

A table's declared composite indexes MUST be part of its `SchemaVersionId` under the `jazz-schema-v2-composite-indexes` id domain, used only when some table declares one so every plain schema keeps its frozen v1 id. Each distinct column list MUST become one SQLite index `<table>__ix(<columns>)`, leading with the branch key on branched tables and ending with `id`. Column order inside an index is identity; declaration order of distinct indexes MUST NOT change the id, hash, equality, or stored layout, and a composite index subsumes a single-column index on its prefix.

A version's content and its deletion state MUST be one stored row, with no separate deletion table: the deleted bit of `_st` marks a deleted version, which keeps the content it hides, and its no-content bit marks versions whose commit wrote no content.
A current read MUST return the current table's rows with `_st < 2` (deleted bit clear); only an `includeDeleted` read of a plain root also returns deleted rows.

A replica's local read MUST read its current table, where its pending writes have replaced the settled images they override (kept aside in its history table as the upstream baseline below the replica's local sequence range), so a read needs no per-row version selection.
A current read MUST be answered from the current table; as-of and history reads read `<table>__h` by its key, and a snapshot keeps reading the rows it froze after later writes.
Changes after a seq MUST be found through the current table's `_seq` index (`<table>__by_seq`), so a resumed subscription reads and ships only rows changed after its seq.

Deleted rows MUST be excluded from every source a query reads (root, joined, included, gathered and policy-evidence rows) before its filters, joins and traversals apply, unless the read includes deleted rows.

A cold subscription's first result MUST read the current table only, so its cost follows the number of current rows, not the depth of their history.

The work to apply and deliver a change MUST follow the results it affects, not the number of open subscriptions, sessions, holders or history depth: unrelated subscriptions are not refreshed, and a caught-up resume ships nothing.
`Query::validate` MUST stamp a shape with the schema version it validated against, and `ShapeId` MUST include both canonical query bytes and `SchemaVersionId`.

An array relation's requirement MUST be part of the query: an optional relation keeps a parent with an empty array, a required one leaves out a parent with no matching child, and an all-resolve forward array leaves out a parent whose references do not all resolve, at the root or nested. Sync MUST NOT drop a readable parent for a relation it has not shipped yet: the relation's rows ship as support.
A local read (LocalFirst or LocalOnly) MUST answer from the rows this node holds plus its own pending writes, complete only relative to what it holds; it never claims rows it has not received.

A settled read on a replica MUST wait until its upstream has answered the query and the replica holds the answer's rows; while the upstream has not answered (offline, connect or auth failure, detached) it stays held rather than answering from partial rows.
A query inside an open serializable transaction MUST record its compiled query and bindings with the result it saw, so the authority can re-run that exact read at commit.

Serializable read validation MUST reject the commit when a recorded read's result under the reader's identity differs between the transaction's snapshot and the commit point (including rows entering or leaving a predicate or window, and rows of deleted or related tables it read), and MUST accept it when concurrent writes leave every recorded result unchanged; a replica's own unsettled writes count as part of its snapshot.
Live results maintained by fan-out MUST equal a fresh one-shot read of the same query over the same state after any sequence of writes.

Changes landing in one refresh MUST be delivered by their net effect on the result: a row that enters and leaves sends nothing, rapid updates deliver the final state, and a transaction's adds and removes of one output are netted.
When a row stays in a result but its version changes, the result member MUST be updated to the new version even if its projected cells are identical.
A serializable commit MUST become visible to a subscriber atomically: its accepted rows reach every result it touches in one delivery, never partly applied.
Semantically identical commutative query forms MUST produce the same `ShapeId`; semantic predicate changes MUST produce a different `ShapeId`.

Row images MUST be deduplicated per peer across all of its subscriptions: a row the peer already holds at a version is not shipped again for another subscription, and a writer's own accepted write is echoed back as fate and settlement only unless the authority's image may differ from the writer's (INV-SYNC-53).

Array relations MUST stay distinct from forward includes and MUST be assembled into nested values inside the query result: every carrier (one-shot, subscription, sync, bindings) delivers complete root values, never a separate edge list for the caller to join.
Structured output MUST be an ordered tree: the root order, offset and projection of the query hold at every level, a reset replaces the whole tree, and every nested record carries its own row id.

A flat joined output occurrence MUST be identified by its ordered contributing source-row ids, not by its root row id; maintained delivery MUST address additions, removals, and replacements by that composite occurrence identity.

Every array subquery in a structured result MAY specify a finite child `limit` (zero is valid); omission selects the complete ordered suffix after `offset`. Logical result size MUST NOT be constrained by a transport frame limit: transport decomposition and reassembly MUST preserve the complete logical message atomically.
`BindingId` MUST be derived from canonical binding bytes in parameter-name order, and bindings MUST reject missing, unknown, or type-mismatched params.

An aggregate result member's identity MUST be derived structurally from its group key, and a scalar global aggregate MUST lower to one fixed synthetic identity. Neither the identity nor any delivery decision keyed on it may be derived from, or matched against, a constructed name such as `<table>_aggregate`; filtering delivery by string comparison against a table name is forbidden.

Aggregate output types are fixed by function: `count` is `U64` and never null; `sum`, `min`, `max` are nullable over the non-nullable base type of their input; `avg` is `Nullable(F64)` and stays finite for large finite inputs. Integer and bigint aggregates keep signed public values.

A stored SQL NULL and an omitted value MUST stay distinguishable until the public boundary: an explicit null is kept over a column default, an omitted optional column reads as null, and a non-null value in a nullable column reads back as itself.

A group present with a NULL aggregate, an absent group, and a group whose aggregate value changed are three distinct outcomes the delivered result MUST distinguish. An empty group and an all-NULL group are both present-with-NULL, not absent.

The non-aggregate fields of a synthetic aggregate row — row id, version, provenance, deletion state — carry no meaning. Producers MUST NOT populate them with interpretable values and consumers MUST NOT read them.
A delivered change for an aggregate member the subscriber does not hold MUST arrive as an add, not an update: a grouped member that leaves and returns is added again.

Rows, history and pending uploads MUST persist in the SQLite file; subscriptions, settlement waits and per-peer delivery state are process-local and are rebuilt after reopen. A reopened replica answers local-first reads from its file and re-sends its pending uploads; a fresh remote read needs a new answer from upstream.

Recursive reads (gather queries, recursive relations, recursive policies) MUST use set semantics, so they reach a fixpoint on cyclic edges, include their seed, and stop at a declared depth bound; a cycle in an inherited policy denies only the rows it reaches.
Shape registration MUST reject an AST whose content-addressed id does not match `shape_id`, and MUST park registrations naming an unknown schema version until the schema catalogue arrives.
A one-shot read MUST be served once without installing live delivery, and MUST NOT change what any open subscription receives.

A subscription delivery MUST contain only changes to that subscription's result: a write to a row outside the result delivers nothing, and a change to an included row updates only the members that include it.

A `Subscribe` MUST carry its whole compiled query and bindings, keyed by a subscription id the subscriber chooses; `Unsubscribe` MUST end that subscription's delivery and forget its result, and a later subscribe of the same query starts clean.

On `Subscribe` the serving side MUST run the query for the subscriber's identity and answer with its full current result before any change, so a fresh subscription's first delivery is its whole opening (possibly empty, once settled).
A reset delivery MUST replace the subscriber's whole result for that subscription (members it no longer lists leave) while keeping the order and update category of members that stay.

Live result members MUST be addressed by row id (a flat join by its contributing row ids, a history read by row id and seq) and carry the version they show, so a new version of a member is delivered even when its projected cells are unchanged.

A synced result MUST ship the rows the reader may read that the query outputs or reads (include targets, array children, join and gather edges); rows the query traverses but does not keep, and rows the reader may not read, MUST NOT be shipped.

Opening a serializable transaction MUST fix its snapshot at the newest commit seq this node holds (plus its own unsettled writes); a read the snapshot cannot answer locally waits for the authority rather than reading a later state.
Current-row visibility MUST be the current content anti-joined with the current deletion state: content writes alone MUST NOT restore a deleted row, while a restore reveals its current content.
A LocalFirst read on the writer MUST include its own pending writes at once, while a Remote read MUST withhold them until the authority has accepted and settled them.
Each current table MUST hold, per (id, branch key), the newest accepted version, and its history table every accepted version; both MUST agree after reopen.

A snapshot MUST cover exactly the versions at or below its commit seq plus the unsettled writes it names; a snapshot captured offline names its unsettled writes and keeps them after they settle, an online capture waits for them to settle.
Reads inside an open serializable transaction MUST see each row as of the snapshot (from history when it changed since) and MUST NOT observe later writes.
Reads inside an open transaction MUST overlay that transaction's own staged writes on top of its base view.
A serializable read MUST be recorded whether it found rows or not, so an absent row that appears before commit conflicts as surely as a present row that changes.

`tx_current_rows` and `tx_query` MUST record predicate reads as `PredicateRead` values carrying `table`, `shape_id`, `shape`, `binding_id`, and `binding_values`; whole-table transaction reads are degenerate query shapes.

A node's current row MUST be the authority image with the highest seq it holds for that row, with the node's pending overlay on top for local reads; receiving images of a row out of seq order MUST leave the same current row as receiving them in order.
Current-row reads MUST leave out deleted rows unless the query asks for deleted rows; then deleted rows read with their deletion metadata and stay under the read policy.
As-of reads at a commit seq MUST read each row's newest version at or before that seq from history, and leave out rows deleted as of it.

A read MUST compose its layers by one rule: the top layer holding a row supplies it, live or deleted, and masks the layers below before any predicate or relational operator applies. A replica's pending writes are the top layer over its settled rows; a branch view's head is the top layer over its base.

A read's layers MUST follow its tier: a `Remote` read is the authority's result alone, without pending local writes; `LocalFirst` and `LocalOnly` read the replica's pending writes over its settled rows.
An indexed branch-view read MUST give the same rows as the unindexed read: the head masks the base under the index, and changes on either branch reach an indexed subscription.

No stored or sent byte MUST encode that a write's unsettled base is its writer's own: a base names an unsettled commit by its sender's id (only the sender's own may go by how far back it is), and each relay renames bases into names its upstream knows. A replica shows its pending writes over each newer settled image it receives, but a write over a pending write is built on that write alone and never claims the settled images shown under it.

A replica MUST keep a row's settled image while a pending local commit overrides it (in history below the replica's local sequence range), update that image from server images, and on a settle or rejection rebase: restore every shadowed row and replay the remaining pending commits in order. History baselines and pending commits survive a restart; eviction removes history without recording an eviction marker.

A commit from a session MUST be refused whole, with an authorization-denied rejection and none of its rows applied, when any of its writes fails its table's write policy for the identity it is checked as. The author recorded as provenance differs from that identity only through a trusted serving link (INV-RLS-17, INV-RLS-18).

A synced query MUST be served with the root table's read policy compiled into it and its session values bound from the server-authenticated identity, so a client cannot widen what it sees through parameters; each identity's binding is routed separately.
Relay peer links MUST have an explicit relay transport capability and no permission subject; client-to-Core peer links MUST use the admitted client `AuthorSubject` for policy-composed reads.

invariant: The rows a serializable commit writes MUST reach each subscriber in one delivery and filtered by that subscriber's read policy: a reader never sees part of the commit, nor rows of it it may not read.
coverage: partial: per-reader filtering of a serializable commit has no dedicated test

invariant: History and as-of reads MUST be gated by the read policy of the row as it is now: a reader sees a row's versions only while it may read the current row, and loses them when that access goes.
Policy evaluation MUST deny when it cannot establish that a policy holds: a missing or deleted inherited parent, a cycle, an absent claim or a NULL comparison all deny.

A table with no declared policy clauses MUST deny ordinary user reads and writes at the serving authority. An effective permission subject under the reserved `urn:jazz:anonymous` issuer MUST be denied inserts, updates, and deletes before table-policy evaluation. Every table policy set is closed: a missing read, insert, delete, or whole update operation MUST deny; a declared update MAY omit either its old-row or new-row subclause. This decision MUST use the policy-owning schema across schema versions and lens projections.

A write whose recorded author differs from the identity it is checked as MUST come through a trusted serving link (a backend acting for a session, or attributing to a user); the write policy is evaluated for the identity the link vouches for, while the author stays provenance.

An uploaded commit MUST be authorized under its link's authenticated identity: on a session link a different author is refused (attribution requires a trusted serving node) and the write is checked as the link, while a trusted link may attribute and have the write checked as the session it acts for.

A required relation MUST count as resolved for a non-system reader only through rows the reader may read: a parent whose required related rows are missing or unreadable is left out, so the relation cannot reveal rows the reader may not see.
The system identity (the database's own writes, an admin-secret link) MUST bypass read and write policies; every other identity is checked.

A session's update, patch, upsert over an existing row, or transactional write MUST also satisfy the target row's read policy; a hidden target fails without disclosing its cells, existence or policy, and an upsert applies the insert policy only when the target is truly absent.

A read or write policy subplan MUST read every table source it evaluates as raw policy evidence without recursively applying that source table's own read policy. The complete evaluating policy—including filters, joins, authenticated claims, policy branches, inheritance, and reachability—MUST still be enforced fail-closed, and dependency rows MUST NOT thereby become user-visible.

Client mutation staging MUST NOT issue a definitive read- or write-policy verdict from partial local state. Update/upsert read visibility and write policy are enforced by the fate authority against its complete admitted policy inputs.

invariant: External JWT application metadata MUST use the flat JWT payload: every non-registered top-level claim is exposed at `session.claims[<name>]`; `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, and `jti` are reserved transport/security claims; and Jazz MUST NOT specially interpret a nested `claims` object.

A row the server evicts as unreadable MUST leave the replica's local reads for that reader, before joins, aggregates and windows, and stay out across reopen until the server readmits it; evicting it never touches the server's own rows.

Session values a policy compares with (the user, the provider subject, other claims, the auth mode) MUST be bound from the authenticated identity and its admitted claims, never from caller-supplied query parameters.
A table policy MUST validate as a query shape rooted at the table that carries the policy.
A server MUST ship a non-system peer only rows its read policy admits, including support rows and deleted rows.

Read-policy revocation MUST remove rows from future settled subscription result sets, and the server MUST evict them so the receiving node drops its local copies (`INV-SYNC-14`). Eviction is coherence, not redaction: it makes no confidentiality promise about data a node already received.
A session's delete MUST satisfy the table's delete policy against the row's current version; deleting a row that is absent or already deleted MUST be refused.
A deleted row and its deletion metadata MUST be readable to a non-system identity only when the deleted row itself satisfies that identity's read policy.

An EXISTS policy MUST require at least one matching proof row for the same identity: a correlated EXISTS reaches the protected row, an uncorrelated one gates every row on the proof set being nonempty without duplicating results, and removing the last proof revokes access. Proof rows are read from committed state, except that a WITH CHECK clause of a write in a commit unit reads committed state overlaid with the unit's other inserts, restores and updates, each contributing its post-transaction content once its own write checks pass, in any order the unit names them. The unit's deletes are not overlaid: a committed row the unit deletes stays visible as committed, and a row the unit both inserts and deletes never counts. A new row is never evidence for itself, and writes of other transactions are never evidence. A unit is accepted only if every such WITH CHECK clause also passes against the unit's full post-state (without the row under check); a write whose policy is monotone in the rows present is re-checked there only when a write grounded with or after it replaced a row's earlier content and so could have taken its pass away: an update, or an insert or restore of a row that was live before the unit.

Chapter 15 MUST NOT describe sharded core as implemented; conforming current implementations MUST treat sharding as an exploratory/open design area. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
A future sharded design MUST keep a global catalogue/sequencer for schema versions, lenses, policy bundles, and the partition-ownership map unless this chapter explicitly replaces that architecture.
A future sharded design MUST define settled positions as per-shard positions or vectors, and MUST specify how `at(position)` and `at_time(t)` resolve across shards.
A multi-shard subscription result MUST NOT be marked complete unless completeness evidence has been obtained for every shard contributing to the result.
Cross-shard permission closures MUST be obtained through shard-core subscriptions or an explicitly equivalent mechanism before a shard-core assigns a fate that depends on remote-shard policy data.

Rebalancing MUST NOT flip partition ownership in the catalogue until the destination shard-core has the partition history needed to serve that ownership and the protocol has defined treatment of in-flight fates/subscriptions.
A future sharded v1 MUST assign every non-global row to a schema-declared shard partition key, and MUST specify behavior for rows without a natural root and rows whose root changes.
Future v1 serializable transactions MUST be single-shard unless a cross-shard serialization mechanism is explicitly specified.
A cross-shard serializable transaction MUST NOT be accepted without validation evidence for every shard touched by its row and predicate read-sets.

A replica MUST apply a message whole: a message larger than one wire frame travels in transport parts whose last part ends it, and nothing of it is visible before the end; a first result or a commit split across frames is applied whole.
A reset after reconnect MUST replace the subscription's whole result (members no longer listed leave) while the server keeps skipping versions the peer is known to hold.
A server MUST ship other peers accepted rows only, never another node's pending or refused writes.
A server MUST apply the peer identity's read policy before shipping any row image, support row or count to it.

When a reader loses read access to a row (through a write or a read-policy change), the server MUST evict it: the row leaves the reader's future settled results and the replica drops its local copy. Local copies are not a redaction boundary, so the eviction is about coherence, not secrecy. This includes rows the replica's own accepted commit wrote and cannot read (a write-only insert): the commit's fate reports its acceptance.

A serializable commit MUST be decided and applied whole at the authority and reach replicas whole: no replica shows part of a serializable commit, and a commit through a relay is decided once by the authority.
Mergeable writes MUST apply per column without waiting for other writes: concurrent writes to different columns both survive, and a later accepted write to the same column wins by arrival.
A row image MUST carry its deleted flag, so a replica can tell a deleted row from one it was never sent, including for rows it cached from an ended read.
A replica's synced result MUST equal the authority's read of the same query for that reader after any interleaving of writes, entering and leaving rows included.
Wire messages MUST name nodes by UUID, authors by identity and schemas by version id; node-local codes (interned author codes, rowids) never leave their database.

A serving peer MUST reject a capability-gapped live subscription with `SyncMessage::SubscribeRejected` addressed to the requested `SubscriptionKey`; the rejected subscription MUST NOT become active, `Unsubscribe` for it is a no-op, and the connection MUST keep serving other subscriptions.
A fresh subscription MUST receive its whole result; only a resumed one, whose client held it settled through a seq, may be sent just the rows changed after that seq.
A resumed subscription served only its changes since the seq it held MUST leave the replica with the same rows as a fresh subscription to the same query.

A receiver that finds an update naming a held row whose body it no longer has MUST reopen that view without known state, and the serving peer MUST then resend every row of the view with its body under ordinary read policy. There is no per-version fetch: rows are identified by `(row, row_seq)` and resent whole. A second such update for the same view before it settles is a protocol error rather than a resend loop.

Per-session delivery state (which versions a peer holds, its subscriptions) MUST live only in the serving process and be released on disconnect; it is never persisted, and session churn does not grow the server.
Results MUST travel as rows and be assembled into result trees by the receiver: no result-tree operations or relation edges travel on the wire.

A replica MUST treat a subscription as settled only when its connected upstream has confirmed it with a settled seq; while the upstream is unanswered, offline, failing or detached the subscription stays held, and a node with no upstream settles locally.

A downstream subscription MUST synchronize canonical authored facts with their logical table, row, transaction, authored schema, branch/source, fate, and witness identity intact under a closure manifest whose epoch, per-class inventory, and digest prove exact completeness; a projected application/terminal row is never replicated truth.
implementation: planned canonical witness-closure sync ingress and manifest validation

invariant: A receiver MUST select history/current and branch-overlay winners in authored lineage before projection, decode every fact under its authored schema, project it through the ordered lineage into the binding read schema, and run local IVM to derive terminal output. It MUST NOT supplement that residual program from unrelated local history. Raw bytes MUST NOT be relabeled as another schema and peer sync MUST NOT introduce `ProjectedAppRow` or an equivalent carrier.

invariant: The serving authority MUST own visibility, membership, and settlement. It MUST ship the complete safe canonical witness closure plus identified authorized residual program for that reader/policy/binding/branch, using stable opaque admission facts rather than hidden evidence where policy disclosure would be unsafe. An opaque admission MUST be rejected if replayed across a different authority lineage/epoch, manifest, shape/binding/read view, reader/policy revision, branch/SnapshotRef, residual-program identity, protected output/source occurrence, or concrete content/deletion/witness version and layer.

Reconnect, exact class repair or reset, and recovery MUST re-establish that closure and local IVM quiescence before settlement.

Native data is durable; scope, terminal state, settlement and resume cursors are volatile. Crash recovery restores no authority scope and requires a fresh remote snapshot.

A strict remote read uses only its fresh exact authority closure; a local-first read may additionally include eligible local pending inputs. Settlement follows complete witness admission and local IVM quiescence.
