invariant: The read protocol MUST be rows plus settlement: the server sends row images, evictions and a settled seq; the receiver installs them and derives every result locally with its own compiled queries. No result sets or completeness facts travel.

Rows MUST be shipped raw, by the authority's stored table and column names, whatever schema version the subscriber declared; a replica mirrors its upstream's catalogue (schema versions, name maps, lens cells) and applies the lenses locally, so an older client still reads rows a newer server syncs.
A replica missing the chunks of a large value MUST request them and install the row only once its chunks are present; a writer pushes a value's new chunks before the commit that uses them.

A Remote read MUST NOT report rows the server's answer no longer lists: rows the replica caches but the answer leaves out (lost access, deletions) are left out of the settled result, while local reads keep them.

A server MUST process a session's messages in the order sent, so a read sent after a commit is served after that commit, including while the ingress limit holds that commit back; only a read that depends on no table the held commits write (nor on any held message whose effect is unknown) may be served ahead of them. A client MUST send its staged commits ahead of the reads asked since its last send.
Applying a fate or a settled seq MUST NOT move a node's settled seq backward or lower a write's reached durability tier; a lost fate is recovered on resume rather than guessed.

A non-durable client's local versions MUST NOT collide with its relay's: every version is stored at the position `(_n, _seq)` of the node that numbered it, so a relay's unsettled versions (shipped with `Image.by` naming the relay) and a non-durable client's (a worker's tab) own writes, each counted from 1 at its own node, never meet; a tab refuses an upstream version numbered by its own node. There is one relay tier (SPEC 9 §9.5): relays are not chained and no durable replica attaches behind a relay. A relay MUST NOT ship a session the versions of that session's own commits it still uploads: the session holds them as its pending writes, so it ships the version they sit on instead, if the session may read that version.

A store that committed writes before it became a replica MUST keep them and refuse every upstream, failing its remote reads (live and one-shot `Remote` ones) and durable waits on its later writes with why: those commits sit at seqs its upstream numbers its own versions by and were never recorded for upload, so syncing would lose them silently. A store that becomes a replica before it writes uploads its offline writes on its first connect.

A replica MUST upload each commit under the schema version whose names its ops use, the version of the schema view that wrote it, keeping it pending while offline, and never resolve it under another version's names. A server MUST refuse a commit under a version it has not deployed at once, with reason `schema_version_not_deployed`, including one behind reads it holds for an unadmitted session version; a relay refuses so only while linked to an upstream whose catalogue arrived on that connection, and re-learns versions an earlier process admitted from it; the session goes on and later commits upload. One commit uploads under one version, so a transaction written through views of different versions is refused. A version made current leaves pending commits under the previous one.

The authority MUST NOT hold back a writer's own row (name it `as_written` in the Fate instead of shipping it) unless the commit applied over the very version the writer built on (its base, the version the writer's own earlier commit landed as, or no version for a row its inserts or unbranched upserts create), no text merge changed what it sent, and that version is still current at fan-out. Every other row ships. Each as-written row carries the authority's digest of its version: a writer whose image differs (stamped as another author, for one), or that holds no image to compare (written under an earlier schema version, or a catalogue with new versions arrived while the commit was pending), MUST ask for the row whole instead of installing it; otherwise it installs its image stamped at the Fate's `accepted_at` where its own clock stamped it. Its fate, and every later one, waits until those rows arrive whole (with the fate's version of each, if superseded), so the commit stays pending meanwhile: a mismatch is one counted fetch, never a divergent cache.

Rows MUST travel as self-contained row images (table, id, branch key, seq, deleted flag, content, cells), and result membership is per row: a subscription never holds a transaction as a unit of membership.

A server MUST track per session which row versions the peer holds and ship each version at most once across all of that peer's subscriptions; a peer it has no record of receives every row its results need.

A receiver MUST reject a `ViewUpdate` that names a `peer_payload_inventory.complete_tx_payloads`, add, or remove transaction it lacks enough tx existence, row-version payload, complete-tx payload, or view-complete serializable payload coverage to resolve for that subscription view.
Randomized differential suites MUST run from fixed seeds so any failure replays exactly.

Node-core simulation must be deterministic: time, randomness, and delivery order are injected by drivers, and failure to replay bit-for-bit is a bug. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
Every consistency claim gets randomized or racing coverage: maintained and synced results against one-shot reads, merge convergence, and serializable validation under racing commits.
The canonical Jazz gate set (appendix D.1) is local-only until CI runs every gate in it. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

Structured-result maintained-vs-one-shot equivalence MUST use canonical `ResultTree` equality, including ordered roots/relations, values, identity, descendants, aggregate/group payloads, and null/hole/empty semantics; root-membership set equality is insufficient.
implementation: planned structured differential oracle and receiver/chunk property

invariant: Canonical-sync reconstruction coverage MUST prove that a receiver derives its terminal from an authored-schema witness closure rather than a replicated projected row, across manifest/epoch integrity, lineage, branch isolation, policies, relations, aggregate inputs, reconnect/repair, recovery, and deterministic fault injection.
A transaction's staged writes MUST NOT be visible to ordinary reads or subscriptions before it commits, and a rolled-back transaction leaves nothing.
A write's reached durability MUST only rise (local, then global), and a wait for a tier the node can never reach fails instead of hanging.

The authority MUST give accepted commits a strictly increasing commit seq, stored in the same SQLite transaction as their rows, before it sends any fate; after reopen it continues above the highest seq it stored.
Local durability MUST NOT imply upstream survival: a write held only locally waits for its global tier, is resent after a restart or reconnect, and is lost only if its local file is.
A serializable transaction MUST capture the newest commit seq this node holds as its snapshot; a read the replica cannot answer from it asks the authority for that same snapshot.
Serializable snapshot reads MUST stay stable after later commits and record what they read, deleted rows and absent rows included.
Reads inside a serializable transaction MUST observe that transaction's own staged writes.
The authority MUST refuse a serializable commit when a row it read has changed or been deleted since its snapshot, including reads made through a schema view whose names differ from the stored ones.
The authority MUST refuse a serializable commit when a row it read as absent has since become present.

The authority MUST refuse a serializable commit when re-running one of its predicate reads, as the transaction's identity, returns a different result than at the snapshot (a phantom entering, a row leaving), and accept it when unrelated writes leave the result unchanged.
Serializable read validation MUST re-run each recorded read with its own bindings, from the query the commit carries, under the schema version it was read with.
Committing on a replica MUST apply the transaction locally as pending, record its upload in the same SQLite transaction, and send it upstream as one Commit.

Serializable writes MUST be first-committer-wins: a write whose base version is no longer the row's current version conflicts, a blind write over an unchanged row is accepted, and a commit over the writer's own unsettled write is accepted.
Each accepted commit MUST update the current tables and append to the history tables in the same SQLite transaction, so every accepted version is in history at its seq.
A replica MUST make a commit's rows visible only once all of them have arrived (frames, chunks); an incomplete commit stays invisible.

Only the authority MUST decide fates. A relay (a worker serving tabs, a backend) stores a downstream commit as pending, forwards it upstream, and assigns no seq and shows it at no global tier until the authority's fate arrives; a relay without an upstream settles its tabs locally.
A transaction handle MUST name the same work wherever it runs, and MUST be terminal after commit or rollback: any later operation on it is refused.

A local commit MUST be one SQLite transaction: its rows, history and upload record land together or not at all, so same-tick reads see the whole commit, a storage failure rolls it back whole with its own error, and a reopen after a crash shows exactly the committed prefix.

Client-side mergeable mutation staging MAY validate structure, schema, locally required preimages, and transaction consistency, but MUST NOT reject from a local read- or write-policy evaluation. The fate authority alone issues the definitive authorization verdict from complete admitted policy inputs.
implementation: planned client staging / authority admission separation

invariant: A commit MUST reach the authority and be applied whole however the transport splits it; the authority decides all of its writes together or none.
A commit the authority already decided MUST be idempotent: a resent copy (after a restart between apply and acknowledgement) gets the recorded fate and is not applied again.

A server MUST hold every message of a session whose declared schema version it has not admitted, deciding none of its commits, until that version is admitted; a read it cannot serve is refused with the reason, and a local writer on an unpublished schema is refused.
coverage: partial: holding a commit until admission has no direct test

invariant: A write MUST carry the base version of the row it was made over. The authority orders writes by its own commit seq, never by writer clocks: a later accepted write overrides earlier ones whatever its clock, and a write is never refused because the writer's clock is behind.

A writer's clock MUST only stamp provenance: a clock ahead of the authority gains its write no precedence, and explicit timestamps reach the authority per write as metadata. A session write whose explicit timestamp exceeds the authority's clock by more than `SKEW_TOLERANCE_MS` MUST be rejected (`client_clock_too_far_ahead`) and MUST NOT leave visible rows.

When the authority refuses a transaction, its effects MUST leave the originating node's local view as soon as the refusal arrives, the row reverting to the authority's version, while the node's other pending writes stay and settle by their own fates; a refusal cascades only to writes built on the refused one (INV-HIST-20).

Originating nodes MUST retain rejected local payloads in retry storage and remove the rejected versions from their rows and history; relays and authorities MUST NOT retain foreign rejected payloads. A store whose host reports refusals keeps each refused commit's payload, durably and across a reopen, until the refusal has reached the application; a refusal no listener took is reported again when one arrives, and a reopened store's kept refusals once its host tracks refusals again. The originating node MUST report each refused transaction to the application with its reason, naming the transaction even when the tab that made it has closed; other nodes never receive refused writes.

A wire-protocol v6 `WireFrame`, its reassembled semantic channel message, each WebSocket frame batch, and each independently versioned v1 NAPI/WASM binding payload MUST be exactly one complete postcard value: malformed, unsupported, corrupt-compressed, fragmented, or trailing-byte input MUST be rejected at its owning boundary before it can acquire a second interpretation. `WireHello.authority.node` MUST use postcard's length-prefixed 16-byte `NodeUuid` representation and be consumed before the exact-frame EOF check. Frozen frame, Hello, semantic-payload, branch/catalogue/large-value, and binding corpus cases MUST decode independently and re-encode to their exact approved bytes.

Every wire tagged union is closed and strictly decoded within a wire version; additive variants, messages and error codes are emitted only behind a negotiated feature bit. Across wire versions only the `Hello` tag plus `min_protocol_version`/`max_protocol_version` prefix and the complete `Error` frame with its baseline codes and retries are shared: a receiver MUST read a Hello's version range before its version-scoped body and answer a foreign range with `UnsupportedProtocolVersion`/`Never`, never `MalformedFrame`.
